relations.subject: Ajahn Sumedho
relations.evidence: He then did a BA in Far Eastern studies and graduated in 1963 with an MA in South Asian studies at the University of California, Berkeley.

relations.subject: Ajahn Sumedho
relations.evidence: From 1967 to 1977 at Wat Nong Pah Pong, he trained under Ajahn Chah. He has come to be regarded as the latter's most influential Western disciple.

relations.subject: Ajahn Sumedho
relations.evidence: In 1975, he helped to establish and became the first abbot of the International Forest Monastery, Wat Pa Nanachat in northeast Thailand

relations.subject: Ajahn Sumedho
relations.evidence: This became Cittaviveka Forest Monastery in West Sussex. Ajahn Sumedho was granted authority to ordain others as monks shortly after he established Cittaviveka Forest Monastery.

relations.subject: Ajahn Sumedho
relations.evidence: Until his retirement, Ajahn Sumedho was the abbot of Amaravati Buddhist Monastery near Hemel Hempstead in England, which was established in 1984... retired in November of that year.

relations.subject: Ajahn Amaro
relations.evidence: Ajahn Sumedho's imminent retirement was announced in February 2010, and he retired in November of that year. His successor is the English monk Ajahn Amaro

relations.subject: Ajahn Sumedho
